scenes.say: Las Vegas. The brightest race of the season, and the slipperiest. Why?
It's a night race, and November nights in the desert are cold, with the air at around ten to fifteen degrees.
F1 tyres are built for heat. Cold rubber grips less, and the surface tears into little rolls of rubber.
The lap is over six kilometres: long straights down the Strip and slow ninety-degree corners.
That's why softs shine here, hards may never get up to temperature, and every restart becomes a lottery.
Follow every driver's tyres and gaps live on LapRadar.

title: Las Vegas: the brightest race of the season, and the slipperiest
